questions.topic: How a wait after the last keystroke shapes a request curve
questions.stem: A debounce implementation calls the handler on every keystroke and cancels the previous timer. What is wrong?

options.text: It requires a Promise
It leaks memory from cancelled timers
It blocks the main thread
It fires on every keystroke instead of after the pause

questions.explanation: Calling the handler on every keystroke defeats debounce. The handler should run only after the timer expires without reset.
questions.hint: Handler runs after the pause, not during typing.

questions.topic: One query per row of a result set
questions.stem: How does eager loading resolve an N+1 problem?

options.text: It caches each row after the first fetch
It fetches related rows in the initial query via a join or batch
It defers all queries until render
It runs queries in parallel threads

questions.explanation: Eager loading retrieves related data upfront, avoiding per-row queries. It is not caching, deferral, or threading.
questions.hint: Fetch related data upfront.

questions.topic: Paging by offset after a row above the page is deleted
questions.stem: Why is cursor-based pagination more stable than offset after deletions?

options.text: It skips deleted rows automatically
It sorts rows randomly
It anchors to a row value, not a numeric position
It uses smaller page sizes

questions.explanation: Cursor pagination resumes after a known row value, so deletions do not shift the window. Offset positions shift.
questions.hint: Anchor to a value, not a number.

questions.topic: Matching a host against an allowed source
questions.stem: A server reflects the request Origin header back as Access-Control-Allow-Origin. What is the risk?

options.text: Cookies are automatically included
The browser caches the origin
Preflight requests are skipped
Any origin is accepted, defeating CORS protection

questions.explanation: Reflecting Origin allows any site to read responses, nullifying CORS. Proper allowlisting is required.
questions.hint: Reflecting Origin trusts everyone.

questions.topic: A stored value written into the page as markup
questions.stem: Which defense best prevents stored XSS when rendering user content?

options.text: Input validation alone
options.misconception: validation does not stop all payloads

options.text: Context-aware output encoding on render
Using POST instead of GET
options.misconception: confuses transport method with output safety

options.text: Storing content as JSON only
options.misconception: storage format does not guarantee safe rendering

questions.explanation: Output encoding at render time is the primary defense. Input validation helps but is not sufficient alone.
questions.hint: Encode on output, not just input.

questions.stem: Beyond disabling the button, what server-side mechanism prevents duplicate order creation?

options.text: A longer session timeout
An idempotency key unique per submission
Rate limiting per IP
options.misconception: rate limits do not dedup identical requests

options.text: Caching the response
options.misconception: caching does not prevent duplicate writes

questions.explanation: An idempotency key lets the server recognize and dedup a repeated submission. Rate limits and caching do not.

questions.stem: For a hashed bundle file, which Cache-Control is appropriate?

public, max-age=31536000, immutable
max-age=0, must-revalidate
private, no-cache

options.text: Disabling the fallback font
Loading the font in an iframe
options.misconception: iframes do not help font metrics

options.text: font-display: optional or swap with matched fallback metrics
